decisions.statement: The model runs in this process rather than behind a socket.
The model is loaded once and kept for the life of the process.
The model files sit beside the parser model page.
A batch has sixteen sentences unless the caller says otherwise.
A sentence is parsed on a single thread unless the caller states a thread count.
The model runs slower across every core than on a single thread.
A thread beyond the first costs more time than that thread saves.
A tensor is disposed of whether the run answers or throws.
A class the model does not name is read as the other class.
No process outside this process is started to parse a text.
A text parsed before is answered from the cache rather than by the model.
A text the model reads is written to the cache as a side effect of that reading.
A head's confidence is taken over the heads its own sentence offers.
The cache is keyed by the shape a parse has as well as by the model.
A parse stored under an earlier shape is read as no parse.

definition: the parse a trained model gives for a text
